description: HER ORBITX es un equipo enfocado en la innovación tecnológica y la exploración espacial, cuyo objetivo es desarrollar soluciones de software que contribuyan a la seguridad y el bienestar de los astronautas durante sus misiones espaciales. A través de nuestro proyecto, buscamos crear un sistema inteligente de monitorización de la salud capaz de supervisar indicadores fisiológicos, analizar datos en tiempo real e identificar posibles anomalías.
summary:
AstroVital: Intelligent Health Monitoring for Space Exploration

AstroVital is an intelligent, autonomous health-monitoring platform designed to protect astronauts during long-duration space missions. It integrates physiological sensors embedded in smart spacesuits and Portable Life Support Systems (PLSS) with an interactive software platform that collects, analyzes, and tracks vital health data, including heart rate, oxygen levels, respiratory rate, body temperature, and other critical indicators.

Powered by artificial intelligence, AstroVital identifies abnormal changes and emerging health trends, generates early warnings, and provides personalized guidance through an AI-powered assistant. It also incorporates individual medical records, symptom reporting, historical data analysis, and health scheduling. Most importantly, its local processing capabilities allow it to operate independently of continuous communication with Earth, securely storing data and synchronizing it when connectivity is restored.

By combining real-time monitoring, predictive analysis, and autonomous support, AstroVital aims to help astronauts recognize potential health risks before they become critical, strengthening crew safety, medical decision-making, and human resilience in space. Its modular design also offers potential applications in terrestrial healthcare, extending its impact beyond space exploration.
details:
Project Details — AstroVital

1. How the Project Works

AstroVital operates through an integrated system of physiological monitoring, intelligent data processing, and personalized health management. Its architecture consists of three main components: smart spacesuit sensors, physical health-monitoring stations, and a centralized software platform.

The first component involves integrating physiological sensors into future spacesuit designs and the Portable Life Support System (PLSS). These sensors are intended to collect essential health and environmental parameters, including heart rate, electrocardiogram (ECG), respiratory rate, body temperature, oxygen saturation, suit pressure, oxygen partial pressure, and carbon dioxide levels. An ESP32-based communication module will transmit the collected information to the AstroVital software, including during extravehicular activities.

The second component consists of physical monitoring stations adapted to different environments. On Earth, these stations will support comprehensive health assessments and medical supervision before, during, and after missions. A compact version will also be available aboard spacecraft and the International Space Station (ISS), allowing astronauts to perform periodic health assessments without significantly interrupting their daily activities. Access will be protected through individual credentials or biometric authentication.

The third component is the AstroVital software platform, which integrates all collected information into an individual medical profile. Its interactive dashboard displays current measurements, historical records, health trends, alerts, and scheduled activities. Most physiological information will be collected automatically, minimizing the need for astronauts to enter data manually. Astronauts will only need to report symptoms or subjective experiences that cannot be measured directly by sensors.

2. Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Health Analysis

One of AstroVital's most important features is its artificial intelligence assistant, connected to a specialized scientific knowledge base through a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture.

This knowledge base will incorporate authorized medical protocols, scientific publications, relevant NASA research, and historical astronaut health data. Publicly available information from repositories such as the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) and NASA Life Sciences Data Archive (LSDA) will provide research material for developing and evaluating the system.

The AI assistant will use this information alongside each astronaut's individual medical history to interpret measurements, identify relevant changes, explain health trends, and provide contextualized guidance. Astronauts will also be able to describe physical or psychological symptoms, including fatigue, discomfort, anxiety, sleep disturbances, and concentration difficulties.

For example, if an astronaut reports unusual fatigue, AstroVital can examine available sleep records, physical activity, heart rate, and other relevant measurements to identify changes that may deserve attention. It can then provide general guidance and recommend contacting medical personnel when appropriate. The system is designed to support medical decision-making, not replace physicians, psychologists, or emergency medical protocols.

3. Autonomous Operation and Data Management

A fundamental design consideration is the possibility of communication delays or temporary interruptions between spacecraft and Earth. AstroVital therefore incorporates local data processing and storage capabilities.

The platform will continue analyzing available information, generating local alerts, and providing access to previously stored medical records even when communication with Earth is unavailable. New measurements and reports will be securely stored in a local database and synchronized with authorized medical personnel when connectivity becomes available again.

Each astronaut will have an individual and protected medical record. The system will maintain historical measurements, symptoms, medical appointments, physical activity, sleep information, and other relevant health indicators. By comparing current measurements with previous records, AstroVital will help identify gradual changes that might otherwise go unnoticed. Its alert system will consider abnormal measurements and evolving trends rather than relying exclusively on isolated readings.

4. Health Management and Scheduling

AstroVital also incorporates a health-management module that organizes medical appointments, psychological consultations, physical exercise, rest periods, and routine health assessments.

The platform will maintain records that can be reviewed during scheduled consultations with medical specialists on Earth. Before each consultation, the system will organize the astronaut's accumulated measurements and relevant changes, facilitating a more informed medical evaluation.

This approach strengthens existing telemedicine procedures by providing organized, longitudinal health information instead of relying exclusively on individual reports or isolated measurements.

5. Technology and Development Tools

The proposed system combines electronic hardware, software development, artificial intelligence, and database technologies. The physical prototype will use an Arduino Uno to demonstrate sensor integration, data acquisition, and communication between electronic components. An ESP32 is proposed for the full architecture as the communication and connectivity module responsible for transmitting physiological measurements from the spacesuit and monitoring systems.

The proposed sensor infrastructure includes devices for monitoring heart rate, body temperature, oxygen-related parameters, and other relevant physiological indicators. These components will eventually be integrated into smart spacesuit designs and the PLSS to support continuous monitoring during space operations.

On the software side, Python will support data processing, analysis, and the development of intelligent system components. Database technologies will manage individual medical profiles, historical measurements, symptoms, and monitoring records. An interactive dashboard will display health indicators, trends, alerts, and medical histories, while the artificial intelligence component will use a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture to retrieve scientific information and generate context-aware responses.

For the competition prototype, the team will use an Arduino Uno and electronic sensors, together with manually entered or simulated measurements to demonstrate the system's functionality. This prototype represents the conceptual architecture; it is not a fully operational medical device or a certified spacesuit integration. In the proposed full implementation, data collection would be automated through sensors integrated into the spacesuit, PLSS, and monitoring stations.

6. Creativity and Innovation

AstroVital's creativity lies in combining technologies that are often implemented separately into a unified health-monitoring ecosystem specifically designed for the challenges of human space exploration.

Rather than functioning as a simple wearable monitor, it connects physiological measurements, individual medical histories, artificial intelligence, historical research data, health scheduling, and autonomous operation. Its most distinctive feature is its ability to maintain essential monitoring and analytical functions independently of continuous communication with Earth. This is particularly important for future missions beyond low Earth orbit, where communication delays and interruptions can make immediate medical assistance more difficult.

Another innovative aspect is the combination of objective measurements from sensors with subjective information provided directly by astronauts. This creates a more comprehensive picture of individual health, incorporating physical indicators alongside psychological and behavioral information. The modular architecture also allows the platform to be adapted to different spacecraft, monitoring stations, and terrestrial healthcare environments.

7. Factors Considered During Development

Throughout the development process, the team considered several critical factors to ensure that AstroVital responds to the actual demands of space exploration. Astronaut safety is the primary consideration, which is why the system prioritizes early identification of potentially concerning health changes. Autonomy is equally important, since essential monitoring functions must remain available during communication interruptions.

The team also considered data privacy and security, ensuring that individual medical records are protected through authentication, access controls, and secure storage. Additionally, the platform is designed to minimize interference with astronauts' work, exercise, rest, and mission activities by automating most data collection processes.

Reliability and personalization are also fundamental to the design. The system must minimize information loss during data collection and synchronization while evaluating each astronaut's measurements against their individual historical baselines rather than relying exclusively on generalized reference values. Furthermore, AI-generated guidance must be grounded in relevant scientific literature and authorized medical information.

Finally, the team considered technical feasibility and scalability. The competition prototype must demonstrate the concept using accessible electronic components while clearly distinguishing simulated functions from the capabilities proposed for a complete implementation. Its modular architecture is intended to accommodate additional sensors, spacecraft, monitoring stations, and future mission requirements.

8. Intended Impact and Applications on Earth

Although AstroVital is primarily designed for astronauts, its potential applications extend beyond space exploration. In the Dominican Republic and other terrestrial environments, an adapted version could support personal health monitoring by organizing physiological measurements, tracking daily activity and sleep, identifying changes in health indicators, and providing access to individual health records.

Its architecture could also support future integration with telemedicine services and digital health initiatives, helping improve access to organized health information and facilitating communication between patients and healthcare professionals. By adapting technologies developed for the demanding conditions of space exploration, AstroVital could contribute to more accessible and intelligent health-monitoring solutions on Earth.

Ultimately, AstroVital seeks to contribute to a future in which human health monitoring is more continuous, intelligent, personalized, and independent of constant external assistance. By addressing the medical challenges of long-duration spaceflight, the project also explores technologies that could benefit healthcare systems and human well-being on Earth.
